samples.summary: `willWrite()` runs before the operation's validation, so a mutator that throws still consumes the pending checkpoint and wipes the redo stack
samples.evidence: `updateBlock`, `insertText`, `deleteText`, `applyStyle`, `setBlockType`, `applyBlockStyle`, `insertImageInline`, `splitBlock`, `insertTableRow`, … all call `this.willWrite()` as their first statement and only then call `findBlockInAnyArray(id)` / `findBlock(id)`, which throws `Block not found: ${id}`. `willWrite()` (memory.ts:230-236) unconditionally pushes `pendingSnapshot` onto `undoStack` and sets `this.redoStack = []`. So a write that throws before mutating anything (a stale block id — reachable on the docs paste/merge paths and from `getStore()` callers) leaves an undo checkpoint identical to the current document (a dead Cmd+Z) AND destroys the whole redo history even though the document never changed. `mergeBlock` (line 425-433) and `deleteBlockByIndex` (line 122) deliberately validate first, showing the ordering matters; the rest do not.

samples.summary: An adopted checkpoint in a batch whose body writes and then reverts leaves a dead undo entry on the stack with redo restored on top of it
samples.evidence: In `batch()`'s finally, `wroteNothing` is true when the body wrote and reverted. The `if (!adopted)` guard skips the pop, but on the adopted path the first write already materialized `before` onto `undoStack` via `willWrite()`, so `undoStack` ends with a checkpoint byte-identical to the current document while `this.redoStack = priorRedo` is also restored. The user gets exactly the dead Cmd+Z (and a subsequent no-op redo entry) the rest of this change set was written to eliminate. The adopted/non-adopted asymmetry is only justified in the comment for the *never-wrote* case.

samples.summary: `canUndo()`'s "floor dropped" latch treats any missing mark at a full-looking stack as permission to undo past the initial document load
samples.evidence: When `stack.lastIndexOf(this.undoFloorMark) < 0` and `stack.length >= YORKIE_MAX_UNDO_DEPTH` (a hardcoded 50 that the SDK does not export), the code clears `undoFloorMark`/`undoFloorDepth` permanently and returns `true` from then on. The enumeration in the comment (shift / clearHistory / popped-by-undo) is an assumption about SDK internals, not something checked: any other cause of a missing mark while the stack is at or above 50 — e.g. a real cap larger than 50 combined with `clearHistory()` followed by ≥50 fresh local writes — permanently removes the guard that stops a user undoing `writeFullDocument`, which `setDocument`'s floor exists to prevent (see editor.ts:1100-1103 on what undoing the initial load destroys).

samples.summary: `recomputeLayout({ keepDirty })` downgrades an `undefined` (full-recompute-pending) dirty set to an empty Set, which makes any later un-marked write in the same undo unit paint stale
samples.evidence: `dirtyBlockIds = opts?.keepDirty ? (priorDirty ?? new Set()) : undefined;`. `undefined` means "a structural edit invalidated everything, next pass must be full" and `computeLayout` only consults its cache when the set is non-null. Converting it to an empty Set makes the unit's deferred repaint fully cached, so any store write performed after the in-unit `requestLayoutRefresh()` that neither `markDirty()`s nor `invalidateLayout()`s its block will be measured from the pre-write cache and painted stale. Before this change the interior `requestRender()` left the set `undefined`, so such a write was still covered by a full pass. Today's TextEditor paths appear to mark or invalidate, so this is a latent trap rather than a confirmed stale paint.

samples.summary: `revocableDocStore` memoizes methods bound to the raw target, so a method reference captured before disposal keeps writing after it
samples.evidence: `const bound = (raw as (...args: unknown[]) => unknown).bind(target)` — the returned function closes over the *real* store and performs no `isRevoked()` check when invoked. `isRevoked()` is only consulted in the `get` trap, so `const insert = store.insertText; /* … dispose() … */ insert('b1', 0, 'x')` writes to the shared CRDT after disposal. That is precisely the stale-holder threat model the wrapper's doc comment states it exists for (a holder that captured something before revocation). No current call site destructures a store method (checked `getStore()`/`getDoc()` uses in packages/frontend/src), so it is a gap in the guard rather than a live bug.

samples.summary: `neuterMutations` replaces the async members `paste`/`insertImage` with a sync no-op returning `undefined`
samples.evidence: `(api as unknown as Record<string, () => void>)[name] = noop;` for a list that includes `paste` and `insertImage`, both declared as returning `Promise<void>`. `await`/`void` callers are fine (docs-context-menu.tsx:272 uses `void`), but any caller doing `.then()`/`.catch()`/`Promise.all` on the result crashes with a TypeError on a disposed or read-only editor. The comment asserts "callers only await or ignore", which is true today but is not enforced by the type (the neutered value lies about its type).

samples.summary: A link that has received a fatal verdict keeps polling the backend every 60 s behind the "Link unavailable" screen
samples.evidence: `retry: shouldRetryShareLinkResolve` stops retries on 404/410, but `refetchInterval: SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS` is unconditional, so a query left in the error state keeps re-issuing `POST /share-links/resolve` once a minute for as long as the dead tab stays open, even though the component can never leave the error branch on a verdict.
